Hello, this is Mrs. Carter, the Grade 4 teacher. I am calling all the families today, because our lost and found box is full again. Here is what is in it. There is a blue jacket with no name. It is a small size, so it is probably a girl's or a younger boy's. There are two water bottles, a green one and a pink one. The pink one has the letters S and P on it, so if those are your daughter's initials, it is probably hers. There is also a lunch box with a cartoon cat on it, and a library book. The book is not a child's, it is the school's, so please look in your children's bags tonight and see if one of their books is missing. Everything stays in the box until Friday. After that, the clothes go to a charity, and the library book goes back to the library. Thank you, and have a good week.

My son's class is doing a family museum this month, and every child has to bring an object that belongs to somebody in the family. We looked everywhere. My wife's family keeps everything, so her parents' house was the obvious place. In the end my son chose my father's old camera. It isn't mine and it isn't his. Technically it is my mother's now, because my father gave it to her before he retired. My son's job was to find out the story, so on Sunday he called his grandparents. It turns out my father bought the camera on his first trip abroad, and he took every family photo with it for thirty years, including our wedding photos. My son wrote all of that on his worksheet. Then his teacher asked whose idea it was, and he said: mine. Which is true. I only drove.
